personas.name: Mark — the time-poor restocker
personas.context: 45, parent of two young children in Islington. Does the household's weekly grocery order late on Sunday night after the kids are asleep. Ocado is the locked-in main shop; GreenBasket is a supplementary order for veg, meat and bakery that he places 'when I have the energy'.
goals: Recreate last week's order with two or three changes in a couple of minutes
Know whether delivery lands in the morning or afternoon so it fits the household's week
Decide for himself what happens when an item is out of stock
Get a simple monthly impact summary he can show his wife without reading a methodology page
frustrations: Spends eleven minutes every week searching and re-adding the same core items because there is no reorder or favourites list
Had chicken thighs silently swapped for drumsticks with no message, which broke the recipe and made him cancel for a month
A delivery day shown only as 'Monday' is not a window he can plan around
A two-day wait feels long against Ocado's same-day, and the Impact Score asks him to do homework
personas.quote: It’s not a significant gap. It’s a deal-breaker.
grounded_in: Delivery silence hurts more than delivery speed
Superior produce is buying patience the UX keeps spending

personas.name: Sarah — the values-driven explorer
personas.context: 31, works in marketing at a B Corp in London. Splits shopping across GreenBasket, Abel & Cole and Sainsbury's and has built a spreadsheet comparing them, hoping to consolidate onto one service. Orders GreenBasket every week to ten days and cares deeply about the mission.
goals: Be inspired while browsing — seasonal produce, new producers, editorial picks — not just work from a list
See the story of who makes the food while shopping, and share a producer with a friend
Watch her personal impact accumulate over time (producers supported, food miles, waste avoided)
Consolidate her grocery shopping onto GreenBasket alone
frustrations: The catalogue is an uncurated grid with no editorial layer, and the homepage never changes
Producer stories that would sell the food are buried in the blog and there is no shareable producer profile
An Impact Score of 73 has no context, no breakdown, and tapping it does nothing
Still has to search for each of her six regular items one at a time, every week
personas.quote: it was like someone had built a gorgeous storefront and then put a spreadsheet inside it.
grounded_in: Browsing strips out the market narrative
Delivery silence hurts more than delivery speed
Superior produce is buying patience the UX keeps spending

actions: Realises there is no booked slot the way Ocado has one
Opens the app on a phone late in the evening when there is finally time
friction: No recurring slot or reminder anchors the order
Competes with the only free hour of the evening
Order happens 'when I have the energy', not on a rhythm

journey.stage: Rebuilding last week's basket by hand
actions: Searches 'eggs', adds; searches 'milk', adds; repeats for every core item
Digs into order history to remember what the basket usually contains
friction: Eleven minutes to reassemble a near-identical order
No reorder button, no 'my regulars' list
The same manual rebuild every single week

journey.stage: Looking for something new to buy
actions: Opens the homepage and browse categories hoping for seasonal picks or a new producer
Finds the same unchanged grid and retreats to the search box
friction: No curation, seasonality or editorial layer
Producer stories hidden in the blog, unreachable while browsing cheese
Nothing about a producer is shareable with a friend

actions: Searches manually for replacements, guessing at what is close enough
friction: Adds another five to ten minutes of guesswork
No way to say 'just leave it out' cleanly

journey.stage: Checking out and choosing a slot
actions: Taps the Impact Score expecting a breakdown
friction: The slot is a whole day ('Monday'), not a morning or afternoon
Impact Score gives no context and nothing happens on tap

actions: Plans the week's meals around the expected day
friction: Delays arrive with no proactive message — 36 hours of silence in one case
No confidence about what time on the day the box will come

actions: Unpacks the box and finds an item was silently substituted
Contacts support, gets a credit, and weighs whether to keep using GreenBasket
friction: The swap was made with no notice and no choice
The substitute breaks the recipe or meal it was bought for
Support handles it well but the trust damage is already done

hmw_statements.statement: How might we let a returning shopper recreate their usual basket without rebuilding it item by item?
How might we make an out-of-stock item a decision the shopper makes rather than one made for them?
How might we give shoppers enough confidence in delivery timing to plan their week around an order?
hmw_statements.derived_from: Delivery silence hurts more than delivery speed

hmw_statements.statement: How might we help a browsing shopper encounter the people and the seasonality behind the food the way a market does?
hmw_statements.derived_from: Browsing strips out the market narrative

hmw_statements.statement: How might we make the impact of shopping this way something a person can feel without studying it?
